title: fix(plugin-security)!: a predicate write composes the platform ownership floor per row, as the by-id write does
body:
repo:objectstack#7 · os-tesla · session_01L9qibvVRcFWKrfWeG5jzPb

Part of #35802 (the `controlled_by_parent` half of the card's repro is left for a decision, see Acceptance notes)


Clause-②: no (narrowing)
Metadata-protocol: none
Skills-docs: none — `skills/objectstack-data/rules/security.md` (lines 69–70) already teaches that a `check` is judged on every row a `multi: true` update writes and one failing row refuses the write; no skill teaches that a predicate write skips rows the caller did not create.

## 维护者速读

- 业务用户用条件批量修改或删除（流程、脚本、服务端批量更新）时，拥有「修改全部」的经理、不是创建人的记录负责人、以及被授予「编辑」共享的人（仅修改），现在能改到他们逐条修改也能改的那些记录；以前只改到自己创建的记录，结果照样报成功。
- 属于记录级权限，替在 18.6.0 上搭审批对象的外部开发者解决「批量改悄悄少改」的问题，延续之前逐条修改那次修复；两页权限文档同步改正。
- 这是一次需申报的收紧：新纳入的某一行若不满足检查规则、或在删除前被拦截规则拒绝，整次批量修改或删除会被拒、一行都不动，以前会只处理创建人的那几行并报成功；普通成员批量改大量别人的记录会变慢（一万行约五秒）。出问题可以直接撤回本 PR，不涉及数据迁移。
- 要你定一件事：新纳入的行被检查规则或删除拦截拒绝时整次拒绝（本 PR 现状，已按收紧申报），还是改为跳过该行只处理其余的。

## What changes

`packages/plugins/plugin-security` only. The #5492 floor composition (the sharing service's `allow` replaces the platform's own `owner_only_writes` / `owner_only_deletes`; `abstain` and `deny` keep it) now runs per matched row on the PREDICATE write path, which never reached it because it sits under `extractSingleId(opCtx) != null` in step 2.7.

- **Step 3, RLS injection** (`security-plugin-authz-middleware.ts`). For an addressed predicate update or delete (`addressedPredicateWrite`) by a non-delegated caller, after the existing read question (`readableRowsScopeForPredicateWrite`, the readable ids the caller's predicate matches, capped at 10,000 with a refusal above), when the platform floor is in play for the caller (`predicateWriteFloorRelief`):
  1. `replaced`: `computeLayeredRlsFilter` with `dropPlatformOwnershipFloor`, the Layer 1 the by-id write of a row composes once its floor is replaced. Where it is not null, an authored `using` policy remains, and the relief answers null with no read and no verdict. Policies compose by OR only, so a row `floored` refuses fails every authored policy too, and its by-id write is refused as well: replacing the floor can add no row there (L2 S2);
  2. one read, under the caller's context, of which matched ids the floored Layer 1 already admits; nothing is asked about them;
  3. for every other matched id, the by-id gate's own floor decision, `resolvePreImageFloorDrop` (`predicateWriteFloorDropIds`, new in `security-plugin-sharing-verdicts.ts`, asked in batches of 25);
  4. Layer 1 becomes `floored OR id IN dropIds`. Layer 0 is recomposed exactly as it stood.
- **Step 3.6, the per-row `check`.** A predicate update's row whose floor step 3 replaced is held to the check `computeWriteCheckFilter` composes with `dropPlatformOwnershipFloor` (what step 2.7 passes for a by-id `allow`); every other row keeps `checkParts`. Without this the floor's `using`, defaulted as the check, refused on the new row the write it had just admitted (ablation leg 2 below).
- **Docs.** `content/docs/permissions/permissions-matrix.mdx` and `content/docs/permissions/sharing-rules.mdx` said that `modifyAllRecords` does not lift `member_default`'s owner-scoped write policies on an ordinary business object, and that members stay owner-scoped on writes even under `public_read_write`. The first has been false by id since #5492, and this PR makes it false by predicate too. The second has been false for update since #8023. Both pages now say: the floor is creator-only (`created_by == current_user.id`). Under `public_read_write` the update floor does not apply and the delete floor does; with no `owner_id` both apply. Where record sharing enforces writes (an `owner_id` and a `private` or `public_read` OWD), the sharing service's `allow` for a row replaces the floor for that row: ownership at write depth or `modifyAllRecords`, and, for an update, an `edit` share. On an update, a row in a queue the caller belongs to gets the same `allow` under any OWD. A by-id write takes the replacement, and so does a predicate write unless an authored `using` policy for the write applies to the caller. An on-behalf-of write keeps the floor. A `controlled_by_parent` detail's by-id write is judged by its master gate. An app-authored policy is never replaced.
- **Changeset.** It declares `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` with a BREAKING banner covering a predicate update and a predicate delete (the FROM and TO, and the fix for a caller), one ADR-0087 disposition (`not-required`, category `no-migration-prescription`), and the measured verdict cost.
- Untouched: Layer 0, every app-authored policy (where one remains, no row is added), the verb boundary (`delete` asks `checkDelete`, and the sharing middleware's bulk delete scope stays owner-only), ADR-0066 ① (Modify All does not skip business RLS on an ordinary object), the delegated path (both floors kept, as on the by-id path), nested predicate writes (no readable-id list, floor kept), and `masterGateCoversThisWrite` (never set on the predicate path).

## Why

#35802, measured on 18.6.0 by an outside builder: a predicate update by a Modify All manager or a non-creator owner changed only the rows the caller created and answered success. Measured on this branch with the fix ablated (= `origin/main` f44758b21e), rows changed by a predicate write over the 4-row owner x creator matrix vs the by-id path:

| caller | verb | predicate, before | by id | predicate, after |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| (a) ALICE, owns r1 r2, created r1 r3 | update | r1 | r1 r2 | r1 r2 |
| (a) ALICE | delete | r1 | r1 r2 | r1 r2 |
| (b) BOB, owns r3 r4, created none | update | none | r3 r4 | r3 r4 |
| (b) BOB | delete | none | r3 r4 | r3 r4 |
| (c) CAROL, created r2 r4, owns none | update | none | none | none |
| (c) CAROL | delete | none | none | none |
| (d) Modify All manager | update | none | r1 r2 r3 r4 | r1 r2 r3 r4 |
| (d) Modify All manager | delete | none | r1 r2 r3 r4 | r1 r2 r3 r4 |
| edit-share target, shares on r2 r3 | update | none | r2 r3 | r2 r3 |
| edit-share target | delete | none | none | none |

## Tests

New `src/predicate-write-floor-deferral.test.ts`, 29 cases, on the `isolated` tenancy posture so Layer 0 is composed on every write: the real `SecurityPlugin` over a real `ObjectQL` + `SqlDriver` (better-sqlite3), the real `SharingService` and its middleware, and the shipped `member_default` floor (the rig of `controlled-by-parent-owner-may-edit.test.ts`). Each case runs the predicate write on one copy of the matrix and a by-id write of each id on a second copy, asserts the two sets are equal row for row, and names the expected set. Cases: the four callers and the edit-share target, each x predicate update and predicate delete (the edit-share delete stays floored: ADR-0111 D3); a Modify All holder under an authored update policy (`stage == 'open'`), which still binds the rows whose floor is replaced; the CONTROL, an owner-less object where sharing abstains, both verbs, where a member still changes only the rows they created; and a row outside the predicate is never touched. Round 2 adds: the verdicts each predicate write asked, recorded on the real sharing service (the floor-admitted rows are never asked about; a delete asks `checkDelete` and never `checkEdit`; no verdict under an authored `using` policy); five on-behalf-of cases (BOB for CAROL, a member with Modify All, both verbs; ALICE for CAROL; ALICE for ERIN, an admin with Modify All, both verbs), each equal to the by-id set; the owner-creator under an authored widener writing the closed row she created, as before; the S1 case below; 60 candidates across three verdict batches; the composed predicate still naming the organization (Layer 0); `idsOfReadableScope` keeping bigint ids; and three direct pins on `predicateWriteFloorDropIds` (the verb it is handed, delegation, at most 25 in flight). The objects are ordinary tenant business objects on purpose: on a tenancy-disabled object a Modify All holder skips business RLS entirely and the floor would never be composed (measured: the first draft of the file used `tenancy.enabled: false` and its manager cases passed for that reason).

A new file rather than a `describe` in `row-write-widener-composition.test.ts` (the #5492 file): that file's engine double cannot run a predicate write's composed AST, the nested read questions, or the sharing middleware's bulk scope, and each of them decides a row here.

## Acceptance notes

- **The admit set is a union; the outcome is not (L2 S1, ruled option (b), declared as a narrowing).** Layer 1 is `floored OR id IN dropIds`: every row it adds is one the by-id path admits for the same caller, and no row today's predicate write matches is removed. But a predicate update applies to all of its matched rows or to none. Measured: ALICE under a check-only policy (`region == 'emea'`), r1 hers and EMEA, r2 hers, created by CAROL, in APAC. Before this PR the predicate update answered success with r1 written. On this head it is refused whole, `PERMISSION_DENIED` 403, nothing written. By id, r1 is written and r2 is refused 403. The same follows from a validation rule, a hook or a `readonlyWhen` lock on a newly matched row. Option (b) keeps the update all-or-nothing and declares it: the changeset carries the BREAKING banner (FROM: success with r1 written; TO: 403 `PERMISSION_DENIED`, nothing written) and the fix for a caller (write those rows by id to get an outcome per row, or narrow the predicate to the rows that pass the check). The maintainer confirms the arm on a decision card, and the PR stays a draft until then. The case is pinned as the declared answer, and ablation A8 below shows the pin goes red when the newly admitted rows skip the step 3.6 check.
- **The delete half of the narrowing (L2 S5), measured.** A predicate delete also applies to all of its matched rows or to none. ALICE's predicate delete over the matrix now matches r1 and r2. With a `beforeDelete` hook refusing r2, it is refused whole with the hook's 409 and deletes nothing. By id, r1 is deleted and r2 is refused 409. A Modify All holder's predicate delete now matches all four rows, and is refused whole the same way. With the relief ablated (A9 below, origin/main's predicate path), both deletes answer success, so both pins go red. A `restrict` relation on a newly matched row refuses the whole delete the same way; that is pinned at the engine in `engine-cascade-delete-atomic.test.ts` and was not re-measured here. The changeset banner now covers delete, and it no longer says a validation refusal comes back the same way as the check's 403 (N7).
- **Measured corner where the two paths still differ, as before this PR:** an owner-creator holding an authored update widener (`stage == 'open'`) on a CLOSED row they created and own. By id: 403, because dropping the floor from an OR of permissive policies leaves the widener alone. By predicate: written, as before. Pinned. Reported as a by-id finding, not copied.
- **Not fixed here: the card's own repro object.** On a `controlled_by_parent` detail, record sharing abstains (except on an update of a row that sits in a queue the caller belongs to) and the by-id write drops the floor through `masterGateCoversThisWrite` (the master gate), which `RlsFilterOptions` documents the bulk path must not set ("a separate decision"). Measured on this branch with the same rig: the master's owner, predicate update over 4 detail rows changes r1 r3 (created by them), by id all 4; a Modify All manager, predicate 0, by id 4. Hence `Part of`. Measured in round 4 with a scratch rig (not committed): a member who sits in queue `q_ops` and may edit the master predicate-updates two detail rows, neither created by them, both with no owner. The one in `q_ops` is written (the sharing service answers `allow`, so the floor is replaced) and the one in `q_other` is not. By id, the master gate admits the row. A member who may not edit the master is refused 403 by the master gate on the predicate write too (`requires edit access to its master record`). So the queue basis never takes a predicate write past the master gate, and the changeset's `controlled_by_parent` line now names this exception.
- **Cost, measured** (SQLite in memory, shared box, one run each; origin/main, then this head). A member updating 1,000 readable rows owned by others: 44 ms with 3 driver reads, then 1,085 ms with 1,000 `checkEdit` and 2,004 reads, writing 0 rows either way. The same at 10,000: 47 ms, then 5,298 ms with 10,000 verdicts and 20,004 reads. A Modify All holder at 10,000: 47 ms writing 0 rows, then 1,796 ms with 10,000 verdicts and 10,003 reads, writing all 10,000. A Modify All holder under an authored `using` policy, 10,000 closed rows: 1,629 ms with 10,000 verdicts at the round-1 head, then 45 ms with none on this head (S2). Bounded by the existing 10,000 readable-row cap, which refuses above it before anything runs. The changeset names all four numbers. The follow-up bulk write scope and verdict contract on the sharing service is its own card.
- Nested predicate writes (a hook's or cascade's own write under the caller's context) are not addressed predicate writes, carry no readable-id list, and keep the floor as before.
- Response shape unchanged: no "rows dropped by the floor" report was added.
- Not taken from L2: N3 (a `!preImageFloorOpts` guard on the relief). Measured on the compare-and-set shape, BOB updating `where: { id: r4, stage: 'open' }, multi: true`: origin/main writes nothing (1 verdict), this head writes r4 (2 verdicts), and this head with the guard writes nothing again (1 verdict). Step 3 does not read step 2.7's decision, so the guard would bring the reported under-write back on that shape. The cost is one extra verdict for one row. N6 (`image.id`) is also not taken: a predicate update never carries a truthy payload `id` (`resolveEngineUpdateDispatch` routes it by id, or refuses), and a falsy one is never in `dropIds`.

## Verification

1. `security-plugin-authz-middleware.ts`, `predicateWriteFloorRelief` (end of file): the union and the floor-admitted read.
2. `security-plugin-authz-middleware.ts`, step 3.6 hunk (`floorDropJudge`): which rows get the floor-replaced check.
3. `security-plugin-sharing-verdicts.ts`, `predicateWriteFloorDropIds`: the per-row by-id decision.

Two-minute check: `pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-security exec vitest run src/predicate-write-floor-deferral.test.ts` shows 29 passed. Flip `if (rlsFilter && layered.layer1 && !delegatorSets)` to `if (false && ...)` and the matrix cases go red.

Round 4 readings are at head `c5208e4597`, and the final head is `35ef59a3ff`. Since round 3 the branch adds two delete pins to the test file and prose in the changeset and the two docs pages. `35ef59a3ff` changes only the banner's first sentence, and the 17 derived families that read a changeset all re-ran at it with exit 0, `check:adr-0087-registration` and `check-changeset-no-major` among them. No package source changed, so the round 3 dogfood battery at `6ff08df403` still reads the same plugin code; it was not re-run. `origin/main` was not merged again, because 4 new main commits would have moved the code the battery read. The round 2 ablations ran on `7b89b3ceb4`, with the same plugin code.

- Batch slice one short, blob `-> 819033e6e42f`: RED, 2 of 27.
